name: IN-08
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+18 district lean in strongly Republican southwestern Indiana
Incumbent Messmer with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
No polling or expert ratings to signal vulnerability
model.rationale: The district's R+18 lean, Messmer's incumbency and roughly four-to-one fundraising advantage over Mary Allen, and markets pricing Democratic odds near 3% all point to a safe Republican hold. No polls or ratings suggest any reason to move materially off the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Allen within single digits or a surge of outside spending against Messmer would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwestern Indiana's 8th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of R+18. First-term incumbent Mark Messmer is running for reelection and holds a clear financial advantage, having raised about $1.2 million to Mary Allen's roughly $295,000, with a similar gap in cash on hand. No independent polls or expert ratings are available for the race, so the picture rests on fundamentals.

Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance of an upset. The combination of the district's strong Republican tilt, incumbency, and the money gap makes Messmer a heavy favorite, with Allen needing an extraordinary shift in the political environment to compete.
